overview: Route-to-Market Distributor Scorecards addresses resource allocation is planned in silos, producing avoidable delays and occasionally infeasible instructions in consumer packaged goods operations. The first proof of value uses sell-in, sell-out and service territory data. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is distributor on-time-in-full score, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: sell-in, sell-out and service territory data; define distributor on-time-in-full score and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Commercial Director / Supply Chain VP.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including replay disruption and edge cases with hard constraints enforced.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
deliverables: Agreed test threshold for distributor on-time-in-full score
